verdict: Avoid new pharma/API exposure in Indore for now — lend only to formulation-led units with clean export documentation and audited buyer books; the fake-NOC export ban on three Indore-Ujjain companies is the deciding fact.
title: Indore Pharmaceuticals & APIs: a note to the credit manager
narrative: Rating reports on peers show the pattern: working capital intensity of 47-52% at Concord Biotech [10], and a small contract-research player at Rs. 61.0 crore FY2024 revenue with heavy US client concentration [8]. So when a proposal lands, check the buyer list and the top-customer share first; if one buyer is above a third of sales, ask for the contract term and the payment history.

## Where cash actually sits
**Cash is trapped in receivables and inventory, and capex is lumpy and approval-linked.** Cohance's fund-based working capital limits of Rs. 420 crore ran at 40-50% utilisation in Q1FY25, down from 70-90%, with term loans of Rs. 152 crore and back-ended repayments starting May 2025 [9]. That is the shape of a healthy unit — moderate drawing power, no big capex pending.

## What has broken now
**The local shock is documentary, not demand: three Indore-Ujjain companies were banned for a year for exporting medicines on a forged African NOC [1].** That is a local news report of 29-10-2026 and it matters more than any macro number, because an export ban stops cash at the port. The state backdrop is soft — MP GST collections -0.1% Apr-to-date against India +6.1% [D] — and India-wide output is -2.1% Apr-to-date while bank credit is +21.6% YoY [D]. Peer results are strong but not local: Aarti Pharmalabs did record revenue of Rs. 613 crore, up 47% YoY, EBITDA margin 22.2% [4][6], and RPG Life Sciences targets 25% API growth [5]. Sources say little about Indore specifically beyond the ban [1][2][3]; lean on first principles and these peers.

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue formulation units selling into domestic trade with audited buyer books, and API makers supplying those units; avoid pure exporters with thin documentation and any unit named in the NOC matter [1].** The growth opening is import substitution — China supplied 65-70% of India's API imports and the API industry grew 8.4% CAGR CY2017-CY2022E, expected ~7% ahead [11]. That favours units adding API capacity for domestic formulators. Rating reports here are undated [8][9][10]; treat them as old.

## How to grow safely
**Structure as working-capital-led: cash credit against receivables, LC-backed import limits, and term debt only against approved capex.** Take monthly stock-and-debtor statements, monthly export-shipment copies with NOC, and quarterly buyer-wise sales. Covenant a minimum current ratio and a cap on top-buyer concentration.

## Early warning signs
**Watch for a sudden export share jump without new registrations, receivable days stretching past the stated cycle, and drawing power falling while sales hold.** Any of these means stop enhancement and inspect documents.
